title: superclaude-tmux-mode
owner: CC gates writes to superclaude and the aider_shim's cocoon integration.
intention: superclaude gains a --tmux argument (with an environment override in the same format as the context-window size override). When tmux is on: CC runs headless in a tmux session, a hook injects 'you've got mail' into each query when mail is waiting, and the shim can detect idle and inject commands (like sailing the next ticket). This is a cocoon part — cheaper stages pre-process, and the shim can drive CC when no human is present.
why: The cocoon pattern (memory cocoon-settle-stages-around-cc): cheaper stages pre-process around CC, and ground truth is the proof. tmux mode is what lets the shim tell whether CC is idle and inject work — without it, the shim has no channel to CC. The mail hook means queued messages (bus mail, probe findings) reach CC without waiting for a human to relay them.
traces_to: Telos 1 — inference compilation: the shim driving CC on idle is the system doing its own work.
Design: cocoon-settle-stages-around-cc — cheaper stages pre-process around CC.
Design: implementation-order-claude-first — CC is the first consumer of its own automation.

falsifier.proves_red: RED on any of: (1) --tmux does not launch CC inside a tmux session; (2) the env var override does not work in the same format as the context-window override; (3) mail waiting and no injection into the next query; (4) shim cannot detect CC idle state when tmux is on; (5) shim injects a command when CC is NOT idle (active human session).

children: none for now — the three pieces (flag, mail hook, idle injection) are tightly coupled and build together
how: Three pieces: (1) --tmux flag on superclaude launcher, with env var override (same pattern as CAIRN_SUPERCLAUDE_CONTEXT_WINDOW). Launches CC inside a tmux session instead of foreground. (2) A hook that checks for waiting mail each query and injects a 'you've got mail' line when present. (3) The shim gains idle detection — if CC is idle in the tmux session, the shim can inject commands (sail next ticket, process mail, etc.).
